info.title: API.SH: Calendar
info.description: The Calendar API from API.SH: public Calendar data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Business days between two dates in a country (and region), skipping its weekend days and holidays: calendar days, business days, weekend days, holidays falling on business days and the list of holidays. Or pass `days` to add (or subtract) business days to a date and get the resulting date.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-business-days

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country: ISO code or English name. See /calendar/v1/holiday-countries.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD; default the first day of this month, or today with `days`).

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD; default the last day of start_date's month).

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Instead of end_date: business days to add (negative to subtract), up to 1000.

parameters.name: subdivision
parameters.description: State, province or region code (e.g. `TX`, `BY`, `ENG`) to add its own holidays to the national ones.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Holiday category: `public` (default) or the country's others, e.g. `bank`, `government`, `optional`, `school`, `unofficial`; comma-separated or `all`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.attribution: Holidays: the open-source holidays project (github.com/vacanza/holidays, MIT)

get.description:
Convert a date between the Gregorian calendar and the Hebrew, Persian (Solar Hijri), Islamic (Umm al-Qura and civil), Chinese, Korean (Dangi), Indian national, Ethiopic, Coptic, Buddhist, Japanese and Minguo calendars: year, month number and name, day, era, leap month, cyclic year and the date written in full and in the native script.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-convert

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Gregorian date (YYYY-MM-DD); default today.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Comma-separated target calendars: hebrew, persian, islamic, islamic-civil, chinese, dangi, indian, ethiopic, coptic, buddhist, japanese, roc, gregorian (default: the main ones).

parameters.name: calendar
parameters.description: Convert from this calendar instead (with year, month, day).

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year in that calendar.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Month number in that calendar (Hebrew: civil order from Tishri).

parameters.name: day
parameters.description: Day of the month.

parameters.name: leap_month
parameters.description: 1 for a Chinese or Korean leap month.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Converts a Gregorian date to the Hijri (Umm al-Qura) calendar, or a Hijri date to Gregorian: year, month number and name, day, and weekday.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-hijri

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Gregorian date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today).

parameters.name: hijri_date
parameters.description: Hijri date (YYYY-MM-DD) to convert to Gregorian instead, e.g. `1447-09-01`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Countries with holiday data: code, name, subdivisions (code and name), holiday categories, languages, weekend days and the years covered.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-holiday-countries

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.attribution: Holidays: the open-source holidays project (github.com/vacanza/holidays, MIT)

get.description:
Public holidays of a country for a year (2000-2035), with the holidays of a state or region when given: date, weekday, English and local name, categories, and whether it is national or which subdivisions observe it. About 250 countries; filter by month and category (public, bank, government, optional...). `subdivision=all` lists every regional holiday. Several years at once with `years` (e.g. `2025,2026` or `2025-2027`) or a date range with `from`/`to`; the answer then also has `years`, `from` and `to`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-holidays

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country: ISO code or English name. See /calendar/v1/holiday-countries.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year (default this year). For several years use `years`, or `from`/`to` for a date range.

parameters.name: subdivision
parameters.description: State, province or region code (e.g. `TX`, `BY`, `ENG`) to add its own holidays to the national ones.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Holiday category: `public` (default) or the country's others, e.g. `bank`, `government`, `optional`, `school`, `unofficial`; comma-separated or `all`.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Only this month (1-12).

parameters.name: years
parameters.description: Several years instead of `year`: comma-separated and/or ranges, e.g. `2025,2026` or `2025-2027` (up to 11 years).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD), instead of `year`; without `to`, up to the end of that year.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive; without `from`, from the start of that year.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.attribution: Holidays: the open-source holidays project (github.com/vacanza/holidays, MIT)

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-is-holiday

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country: ISO code or English name. See /calendar/v1/holiday-countries.

parameters.name: date

parameters.name: subdivision
parameters.description: State, province or region code (e.g. `TX`, `BY`, `ENG`) to add its own holidays to the national ones.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Holiday category: `public` (default) or the country's others, e.g. `bank`, `government`, `optional`, `school`, `unofficial`; comma-separated or `all`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.attribution: Holidays: the open-source holidays project (github.com/vacanza/holidays, MIT)

get.description:
Every stretch of three or more days off in a country's year (weekends joined with public holidays), with the holidays in it, and the longer breaks a single bridge day would create.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-long-weekends

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country ISO code or English name.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Year (default this year).

parameters.name: subdivision
parameters.description: State or region code, to include its holidays.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Holiday categories (default public).

parameters.name: min_days
parameters.description: Shortest break to list (default 3).

parameters.name: bridge
parameters.description: 0 = leave out breaks that need a bridge day (default 1).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.attribution: Holidays: the open-source holidays project (github.com/vacanza/holidays, MIT)

get.description:
The next holidays of a country (and region) from today or a date, with days until each.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-next-holidays

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country: ISO code or English name. See /calendar/v1/holiday-countries.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: How many (default 10, max 100).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today).

parameters.name: subdivision
parameters.description: State, province or region code (e.g. `TX`, `BY`, `ENG`) to add its own holidays to the national ones.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Holiday category: `public` (default) or the country's others, e.g. `bank`, `government`, `optional`, `school`, `unofficial`; comma-separated or `all`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Prayer times for any place and date (up to 31 days): imsak, fajr, sunrise, dhuhr, asr, sunset, maghrib, isha and midnight in local time, with the Hijri date. Computed with the chosen method's published angles (default: the method used in the place's country), Standard or Hanafi Asr, and a high-latitude rule.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-prayer-times

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude. Pass with `lon`; or use `q`, `postal_code` or `geonameid`.

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitude.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Place name, optionally with region and country: `Cairo`, `Birmingham, GB`.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Postal code, with `country` (default US).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country for `q` or `postal_code` (ISO code or English name).

parameters.name: geonameid
parameters.description: GeoNames id of a place (from /geo/v1/cities).

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: First date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today).

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Days, 1-31 (default 1).

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: Calculation method (default by country, else MWL).

parameters.name: school
parameters.description: Asr: `standard` (Shafi, Maliki, Hanbali) or `hanafi` (default by country).

parameters.name: high_latitude
parameters.description: Rule where twilight never ends: `angle_based` (default), `night_middle`, `one_seventh`, `none`.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Times are computed astronomically from the method's published angles; local mosques may add their own adjustments.

get.description:
For a place and date (or up to 31 days): sunrise, sunset, solar noon and its sun altitude, day length, civil, nautical and astronomical dawn and dusk, golden hours, polar day or night; moonrise, moonset, moon phase and its name, illumination, age and distance; and the next new moon, first quarter, full moon and last quarter. Times are in the place's local time zone.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/calendar-sun-moon

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Place name, e.g. London or Paris, France.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude (with lon) instead of a place.

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitude.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Postal code (with country).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country code to narrow a place or postal code.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: First day (YYYY-MM-DD); default today at the place.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of days (default 1, max 31).

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: Observer height in metres (moves sunrise and sunset slightly).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

example.note: Computed astronomically for the location (times in its local time zone, accurate to about a minute; moon times to a few minutes). Phase: 0 n…

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
